citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., & Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. arXiv preprint arXiv:1606.06031.
creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández (University of Trento, University of Amsterdam)
description: A dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task requiring a broad discourse context.
name: LAMBADA
publisher: University of Trento, University of Amsterdam
rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 12 (1 subject in step 1, 1 subject in step 2, up to 10 subjects in step 3)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: In the crowdsourcing pipeline, 84–86% items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2 and another 3–5% at step 3. Only about one in 25 input examples passed all the selection steps.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 1. One subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage. 2. If right, a second subject guessed based on the whole passage. 3. If right, up to 10 subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only (3 guesses per sentence). If no subject was able to guess it, the passage was added to the dataset.
rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely over-represented in LAMBADA (48%), while other categories are under-represented compared to the POS distribution in the input.
rai:dataCollection: Passages were extracted from the Book Corpus, filtered by language models to remove easy examples, and then evaluated by human subjects on CrowdFlower to ensure the target word could only be guessed with broad context.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing 5,325 unpublished novels and 465 million words.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtered out passages that are relatively easy for standard language models (any passage whose target word had probability >= 0.00175 according to any of four language models was excluded).
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluate general-purpose models in terms of how they fare on broad-context understanding.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN) and three models trained on the Book Corpus (a standard 4-gram model, a RNN and a feed-forward model) were used to filter out easy passages.
